nodes.title: Note: Fast Video FastH3
widgets_values:
## FastVideo FastH3 OmniRef

[FastH3 OmniRef](https://huggingface.co/FastVideo/FastH3-OmniRef-Comfy) is FastVideo's reference-to-video checkpoint on top of MiniMax H3: the distilled student (step 3500) trained with trajectory-based PDD and a joint DMD loss, so it renders synchronized video and audio in **8 sampling steps**. VSA is trained on 128-token tiles; ComfyUI runs 64-token tiles and the difference is not visible, since the larger tile only speeds up the native kernel on datacenter GPUs.

## About this workflow

This template runs the **reference-to-video (ref2va)** task with the `MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo` node. Reference images are woven into the packed sequence, so a character, a product or a location can be reused across shots while the model still generates the performance and the audio.

**Key inputs**

- **ref_images**: up to 9 reference images; two are wired here (`<Picture 1>` identity, `<Picture 2>` location). Add more slots on the node if you need them.
- **ref_videos / ref_audios**: optional, up to 3 each. A reference video can carry its own soundtrack.
- **prompt**: address the inputs by tag in connection order (`<Picture 1>`, `<Picture 2>`, …), then describe the shot, the motion and one line of dialogue; the audio follows the description.
- **ref_image_size**: `match` downscales references to the output resolution (faster), `max` keeps up to a 2048px short edge for stronger identity fidelity at the cost of speed.
- **Duration → length**: the `Float (Duration)` value is converted to the 17k+5 frame grid the model expects (5 s = 124 frames at 24fps).

## Required settings

- **Model Sparse Attention** must stay on method `vsa` with `keep_percent` 10: FastH3 checkpoints are trained with VSA and must never run plain block-sparse attention. `sol-attn` and `sla` are not compatible.
- **Model Attention Backend** only picks the dense fallback used before `start_percent` and under `min_tokens`; `comfy kitchen attention` is the int8 kernel.
- **MiniMaxH3SigmaShift** 12 / 3 is this checkpoint's video / audio shift. The FastH3 V2 text-to-video recipe (video shift 10) is not an OmniRef recipe, so do not copy it here.

## Checkpoints

Two diffusion files are published for this model: the int8 convrot export used here (22.2 GB) and a bf16 export (44.2 GB). Load exactly one of them; the text encoders and VAEs are shared with the FastH3 V2 packaging. The NVFP4 AWQ option in the text encoder folder is a text encoder, not an NVFP4 export of this diffusion model.

## Scope

This checkpoint is distilled for reference-to-video. Plain text-to-video works but is not its strength; use **FastVideo FastH3: Text to Video** or **Image to Video** for those tasks.

**vae**

- [minimax_h3_video_vae_int8_convrot.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/vae/minimax_h3_video_vae_int8_convrot.safetensors) (2.62 GB)
- [minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/vae/minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors) (577.2 MB)

**diffusion_models**

- [fasth3_omniref_8step_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/FastVideo/FastH3-OmniRef-Comfy/resolve/main/diffusion_models/fasth3_omniref_8step_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors)

**text_encoders**

- [qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/text_encoders/qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors) (14.61 GB)


## Model Storage Location

```
📂 ComfyUI/
├── 📂 models/
│   ├── 📂 vae/
│   │   ├── minimax_h3_video_vae_int8_convrot.safetensors
│   │   └── minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors
│   ├── 📂 diffusion_models/
│   │   └── fasth3_omniref_8step_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors
│   └── 📂 text_encoders/
│       └── qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors
```

## Report Issue

Note: Please update ComfyUI first ([guide](https://docs.comfy.org/installation/update_comfyui)) and prepare required models. Desktop/Cloud updates follow stable releases, so some nightly-supported models may not be available yet.

- Cannot run / runtime errors: [ComfyUI/issues](https://github.com/comfyanonymous/ComfyUI/issues)
- UI / frontend issues: [ComfyUI_frontend/issues](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI_frontend/issues)
- Workflow issues: [workflow_templates/issues](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/issues)

nodes.title: Input Text (Prompt)
widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is Tran Tich Tac, the adult Vietnamese man defined by <Picture 2>. Preserve his recognizable face, short textured black hair, moderately muscular build, charcoal T-shirt, beige trousers and dark slippers. Expression portraits represent the same person, not additional characters.

<Picture 1> is a four-panel storyboard in a 2-by-2 grid. Read SHOT 1 top left, SHOT 2 top right, SHOT 3 bottom left, SHOT 4 bottom right. Use these as successive full-screen shots.

summary:
A 15-second Vietnamese comedy scene with escalating, expressive anger. Tran Tich Tac scrolls through videos while bouncing his knee on a beige sofa. An absurd story plays from his phone. He becomes furious, slams the phone onto the sofa cushion, then points at it and angrily berates it.

Match the East Asian semi-realistic 3D CGI beauty render style with subtly doll-like idealization in the references.

retention_analysis:
Build from relaxed scrolling to visible disbelief, then a sudden phone slam and an explosive verbal reaction. Make the anger readable through sharply lowered brows, narrowed eyes, a tense jaw and emphatic mouth shapes. Preserve facial identity throughout.

Only Tran Tich Tac appears. Never show the people mentioned in the phone narration.

detailed_description:
Generate four sequential full-screen cinematic shots. Remove storyboard labels, grids, borders, caption strips and drawn motion marks. No subtitles or text overlays.

Maintain the same beige sofa, apartment furniture and warm daylight from screen left. Keep the camera on the same side of the action axis.

00:00–00:02 — SHOT 1:
Wide three-quarter shot matching the top-left panel. A subtle camera push-in. He lounges on the sofa, bouncing his right knee and scrolling the upright black smartphone with his right thumb. His left hand rests on his left thigh. He looks relaxed and faintly amused. His mouth stays closed during the phone narration.

00:02–00:07.80 — SHOT 2:
Cut to the medium close-up matching the top-right panel. Locked camera. His scrolling stops. His brows draw sharply together, eyes narrow, nostrils flare subtly and jaw tightens in mounting anger. His left hand grips his left thigh. His knee stops bouncing. He stares at the phone screen, holding it in his RIGHT hand. He remains silent until the narration ends.

00:07.80–00:08.70 — SHOT 3:
Cut to the medium shot matching the bottom-left panel. Locked camera. He leans forward and angrily slams the phone flat, SCREEN UP, onto the soft sofa cushion immediately beside his RIGHT hip, on screen left of his torso.

Show one continuous action: his right arm moves down, the phone contacts and slightly compresses the cushion, his right hand releases it, and the phone remains there. The phone stays intact. His left hand braces on his left thigh.

At the impact, he sharply shouts:
“Thằng ngu.”

00:08.70–00:15.00 — SHOT 4:
Cut to the medium shot matching the bottom-right panel. Locked camera. The phone remains face up on the same cushion beside his right hip.

He raises his now EMPTY RIGHT hand and points his right index finger down at the phone. Leaning forward, he angrily berates it with deeply furrowed brows, tense cheeks and emphatic speech. His left hand stays clenched on his left thigh.

Say rapidly and angrily:
“Tổng tài mà vì một con không ra gì mà nhịn ỉa, mày không biết tôn trọng cậu mông, tôn trọng đồng tiền à?”

Use two small emphatic downward pointing beats while keeping the finger aimed at the phone. End with a furious glare at it. He remains seated and never picks the phone up again.

Maintain natural hands, one phone and one character. Do not switch hands, duplicate the phone, make it float, or return it to his hand after the slam.

overall_soundscape:
Vietnamese speech only. No overlapping speakers.

00:00–00:07.80:
A very fast, melodramatic Vietnamese narrator plays through the phone speaker with light small-speaker compression. Tran Tich Tac does not lip-sync to this narration. Preserve this exact wording:
“Cô dâu của tổng tài bỏ trốn trước hôn lễ vì ánh trăng sáng của cô ta bị táo bón, tổng tài suy sụp quyết định nhịn ỉa, vì không đi đại trong 6 tháng nên tử vong”.

The phone narration finishes before he speaks.

00:07.80–00:08.70:
One short, muffled phone impact against the upholstered cushion, a sofa creak, and Tran Tich Tac's sharp angry exclamation:
“Thằng ngu.”

00:08.70–00:15.00:
His distinct adult Vietnamese male voice delivers the remaining exact line with forceful irritation and very brisk comedic pacing. Articulate clearly without adding words. Synchronize his mouth only to his own dialogue.

Quiet apartment ambience beneath the voices. No glass breaking, destruction sounds or added dialogue.

non_diegetic_music:
None. No score, musical stings or laugh track.

nodes.title: Note
widgets_values: At full `1344x768` (around 1MP) and `362` frames (15s), VSA sparse attention is about 2x faster than the int8 attention backend; at shorter, smaller clips it offers little speedup. This template uses `120 frames` (about `5s`) just to avoid OOM on some low-VRAM GPUs.
